summary.description: Implement single pending message slot that allows users to send follow-up messages while Annie is processing, preventing concurrent request conflicts and ensuring messages are handled sequentially after completion.
summary.user-story: As a user, I want to send follow-up messages while Annie is working, so that I can add context without waiting for the response.

criterion.title: Processing Flag
criterion.description: Redis key `processing:{user_id}` indicates active request, set to "1" on start, deleted on completion, TTL 3 minutes, atomic operations for concurrency safety

criterion.title: Single Pending Slot
criterion.description: Redis key `pending_message:{user_id}` stores pending messages (newline separated), max 4000 chars, TTL 5 minutes, NOT a queue - single concatenated string

criterion.title: Status Update for Pending
criterion.description: First pending: "📝 Got it - will handle after current request...", Subsequent: "📝 Added to pending ({n} follow-up messages)..."

criterion.title: Auto-Pickup on Completion
criterion.description: After response completes, check pending, atomically clear and process as new request, LLM sees natural chat history flow, recursive handling

criterion.title: Concurrent Request Safety
criterion.description: Only one active processing per user, pending slot prevents races, Redis atomic operations (SETNX, pipeline GET+DELETE)

key.name: processing:{user_id}
key.usage: Indicates user has active request being processed

key.name: pending_message:{user_id}
key.operation: GET/SET for append, pipeline GET+DELETE for atomic retrieval
key.usage: Stores messages sent while processing active

operation.name: Set Processing Flag
operation.description: Atomically set flag only if not exists (NX flag), with 180s TTL
operation.return: True if set, False if already exists

operation.name: Check Processing Flag
operation.description: Returns "1" if processing, None if not

operation.name: Append Pending Message
operation.command: existing = await redis.get(f"pending_message:{user_id}") or "" combined = f"{existing}\n{message}" if existing else message if len(combined) > 4000: combined = combined[-4000:] # Keep most recent await redis.set(f"pending_message:{user_id}", combined, ex=300)
operation.description: Append to existing pending, truncate if too large

operation.name: Atomic Get and Clear Pending
operation.command: pipe = redis.pipeline() pipe.get(f"pending_message:{user_id}") pipe.delete(f"pending_message:{user_id}") results = await pipe.execute() pending = results[0] # The GET result
operation.description: Atomically retrieve and clear pending messages using pipeline

pattern.name: ProfileManager Atomic Operations

example.code: # Use HINCRBY for atomic increment (avoids read-modify-write race) await self.redis_client.hincrby( f"profile_meta:{user_id}", "message_count", 1 )

pattern.lesson: Use atomic operations like HINCRBY/SETNX to avoid race conditions

concern.solution: SETNX ensures only one message processes at a time, others go to pending

concern.issue: Processing flag expires during long request
concern.solution: 3-minute TTL is safety net; normal requests complete faster. Flag deleted on completion regardless.

concern.issue: Race between GET and DELETE pending
concern.solution: Use Redis pipeline to atomically GET and DELETE in single round-trip

concern.issue: Network failure after GET pending but before DELETE
concern.solution: 5-minute TTL on pending ensures eventual cleanup. Duplicate processing acceptable over message loss.

case.handling: Max size 4000 chars truncates oldest, keeping most recent messages
Flag still deleted on completion. TTL is safety net only. New request could start but backend likely handles gracefully.
Message lost. Acceptable tradeoff - user can resend. Prevents indefinite queueing.
Gracefully degrade - allow message through without pending logic. Log error. Follow StateManager error patterns.
Processing flag set during pending processing, so new messages append to pending. Recursive pickup handles.
